summary.headline: Canara Robeco AMC Q1 FY27 revenue from operations rose 20% YoY to INR116.20 crores; PAT grew 24% to INR75 crores.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue from operations was INR116.20 crores (up 20% YoY from INR97 crores) and total income was INR145.80 crores including INR29.64 crores of mark-to-market gains. PAT was INR75 crores, up 24% YoY. Management said quarterly average AUM grew only about 7% YoY and about 1% QoQ, so most of the revenue growth came from higher yields and cost control at scheme level. Closing AUM was about INR1.2 lakh crores, roughly 91% equity and 9% debt. Management guided to an equity yield of 36-40 bps and said the yield would normalise over the next quarter or two.

financial_highlights.change: +20% YoY (from INR121.30 crores); includes INR29.64 crores MTM
Management said yields rose QoQ; company range 35-38 bps
Management said grown in value; SIP accounts declined QoQ

financial_highlights.value: approx. INR735 crores (analyst figure, not disputed)
financial_highlights.change: Skin-in-the-game investment INR176 crores incl. MTM INR65 crores

segments.name: Equity
segments.commentary: Equity yield 39-40 bps in Q1; equity AUM grew about 13-14% QoQ per management, spread across categories. Equity makes up about 91% of AUM.

segments.name: Fixed income / Debt
segments.commentary: Yield 27-28 bps. Debt portion of treasury book (about INR600 crores per analyst, confirmed) booked realised gains of INR8.5 crores on debt, with MTM also contributing to the INR30 crores total.

segments.name: Liquid and overnight
segments.commentary: Yield 2-3 bps; small share of AUM.

guidance_outlook: Equity yield expected in the range of 36-40 bps, rationalising over the next quarter or two as markets stabilise.
Target cost-to-income ratio of around 36-42% (management cited 38-42% and 36-41% at different points); company is well within this range.
Targets about two NFOs in FY27, subject to board and SEBI approval.
A new mutual fund product to launch in the next two to three months; passives and SIF products are on the short-to-medium-term agenda with sequencing.
Strategy remains equity-focused; no ESOP second round timing given yet.
capex_capacity: Ongoing investments in digital platforms, investor experience, operational efficiency, investment team and research capability; no capex figures disclosed.
Passives and SIF launches are under consideration as later-stage product expansion; no timelines beyond short-to-medium term.
demand_pricing: Industry net flows concentrated in arbitrage (hybrid) and small/mid cap equity, per management; Canara Robeco's growth described as more equitable across products.
Quarterly average AUM only about 7% YoY and about 1% QoQ, which management did not explain with specific numbers.
Yield up on TER slab structure (higher TER in downturn) plus scheme-level cost reductions; management would not give segment-wise breakdown beyond yields.
Distributor commissions were said to be negotiated one-on-one; management declined to disclose the structure and said it is competitive but wants funds sold on performance.

Management said SIP AUM grew to about INR41,000 crores even as active SIP accounts fell QoQ amid market volatility and higher discontinuations; reactivation initiatives said to be showing gradual improvement.

qa_highlights.question: Why did yields rise QoQ, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Atit Turakhiya cited TER slab structure linked to AUM, higher TERs during the market downturn, and cost control within TER. Management likes a 35-38 bps yield range. Equity yield expected at 36-40 bps and may normalise over one to two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: How much of 20% revenue growth is from yield vs MTM vs flows?
qa_highlights.answer: Operational revenue rose INR19 crores, and the INR29 crores MTM sits on top of the INR116 crores. Net inflows were not disclosed. Analyst view was about 7% from AUM and about 12% from yield; management did not dispute the split but gave no figures.

qa_highlights.question: Treasury book composition and MTM gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Investments of about INR110.25 crores are skin in the game, with MTM of INR65 crores (total INR176 crores). The rest is in overnight and income funds (debt). INR30 crores in Q1 includes INR8.5 crores realised debt gain plus MTM. Debt gains are booked every quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why did quarterly average AUM grow only ~1% QoQ despite equity strength?
qa_highlights.answer: Gaurav Goyal said industry growth was concentrated in arbitrage and small/mid cap. Company says its growth is spread across products and aims for equitable growth. Management said the goal is to grow AUM and profitability together, without giving a specific number.

qa_highlights.question: Declining SIP accounts and reactivation efforts?
qa_highlights.answer: Gaurav Goyal said higher discontinuations in volatility, with some improvement in the last month. Initiatives with channel partners are in place and results are expected gradually. SIP AUM is about INR41,000 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Cost of ESOP and Q1 cost decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajnish Narula said the existing ESOP program from the IPO is in place, with a second round to be announced later. Atit Turakhiya said Q4 cost included NFO expenses, so a QoQ cost decline is a fair assumption.

risks_watch: Quarterly average AUM growth of about 7% YoY is weak against 20% revenue growth; sustained yield gains depend on TER structure and market levels.
Management expects equity yield to normalise to 36-40 bps over the next one to two quarters.
Active SIP accounts declined QoQ; monitor reactivation results and SIP flows.
Market share loss on a QoQ and YoY basis, as flagged by an analyst; management did not give figures.
Rising compliance costs and investments (AI, digital, new products) could weigh on the cost-to-income ratio.
Passives and SIF launches could lower yields over time; management says costs are not added.
summary.management_tone: Confident on profitability and yields, but evasive on flows, market share, SIP specifics, distributor commissions and benchmark data (deferred to the website). Management said it did not have the figures on hand for several questions.
key_quotes: We like our yields to be in the range of 35 to 38.
Yield for us in our business is certainly an important factor but not the only factor we look at while building our business.
Well, that's the endeavor of the company. We like to see growth.
We generally target about two in the financial year, but they're subject to of course board and SEBI approval.

growth.why: No revenue growth guidance given; Q1 revenue +20% YoY was driven by higher yields and scheme-level cost cuts while quarterly average AUM rose only ~7% YoY and ~1% QoQ. Guidance is limited to an equity yield of 36-40 bps for 1-2 quarters and about two NFOs in FY27 subject to approvals, with no capacity or order backing.
